mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 1% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and real personal savings (RSAFS) increase by more than 5% YoY, it signals a contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS increases > 5% YoY
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS increases > 5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) for three consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is above 3% YoY, it signals a potential overheating economy with loose monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: overheating economy with loose monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 3% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of real personal savings (RSAFS) relative to GDP (GDPC1) indicates a potential for future consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS is high relative to GDPC1.
